issues.description: coerceNumber silently maps null to 0, replacing the prior NaN-propagation behavior of toNumber.
issues.detail: The old panLinear/zoomLinear used toNumber as lift, which returns null for non-numeric input and produces NaN downstream. The new coerceNumber substitutes 0, silently distorting the domain for bad input. This is a real semantic change buried inside a 'just types' PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or document and own the new contract.

issues.description: Public signatures still take number[] then runtime-check non-empty, instead of typing the precondition.
issues.detail: The functions require non-empty domains but advertise number[], splitting the contract between types and a runtime isNonEmpty guard plus throw. Pushing NonEmptyArray<number> (or readonly [number, ...number[]]) into the signature would enforce the invariant at the boundary, make the runtime check a backstop, and align with the new peek overloads. Half-typed is worse than fully typed.

issues.description: Empty-domain inputs now throw where they previously soft-failed with NaN/undefined.
issues.detail: The prior implementation accepted any array; peek of empty returned undefined and arithmetic yielded NaN. The new code throws inside pan/zoom, strengthening the public precondition. Any caller relying on soft-fail breaks. Document this in release notes and the type signature, or make it non-throwing for backwards compatibility.

issues.description: Local identity shadows the previously-imported accessors.identity utility.
issues.detail: The old file imported identity from './accessors.js'; the new file inlines a typed identity and a coerceNumber wrapper. Functionally equivalent, but it duplicates a shared utility and diverges from the codebase voice. Either keep the import and fix the shared type once, or justify the narrower local in a comment.

issues.description: Empty-domain tests only cover panLinear/zoomLinear; Log/Pow/Symlog paths are untested.
issues.detail: The guard lives in pan/zoom so it covers all callers, but panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before delegating, producing sign=NaN before the throw. A small table-driven test over all eight entry points would prove the contract cheaply and catch the ordering sloppiness in the Log variants.

issues.description: peek overload pair is correct but heavier than needed if callers used NonEmptyArray at the boundary.
issues.detail: Two overloads plus an implementation signature for a one-line array[length-1]. The contract is sound, but if pan/zoom signatures enforced non-empty at the edge, peek would not need the overload at all. Worth keeping if other callers rely on the undefined branch; otherwise document the precondition in JSDoc.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR does roughly what it claims — ports transform.js to TypeScript and adds an empty-domain guard — but smuggles in two real contract changes under the 'just types' banner: coerceNumber now maps null to 0 instead of propagating NaN, and empty domains throw rather than soft-fail. Independently, all three reviewers flag that the public signatures still accept number[] with a runtime non-empty check, instead of pushing NonEmptyArray into the type and letting the guard collapse. Secondary cleanups: the inlined identity duplicates the prior accessors import, empty-domain tests cover only Linear, and the peek overloads are sound but heavier than needed if the boundary were typed properly. Verdict: needs-work — own or revert the semantic changes, tighten the Domain input type, broaden the tests.
